title: The Mentalist reads you in one glance
dek: No case to solve, no trivia to remember. Twelve questions and the CBI will decide which member of the team you actually are.

questions.prompt: You walk into a crime scene and immediately notice:

options.label: The thing that is missing
Who is lying, and how badly
The person nobody has spoken to yet
The paperwork that has not been filed
The one who does the impossible bit
The one who keeps it legal
The one who talks to the family
The one who reads the file twice
Understanding the person
Following the evidence

questions.prompt: Where you do your best thinking:

options.label: At a desk that is far too tidy
options.alt: A neat office desk with a chair

options.label: In a café, watching strangers
options.alt: A café interior with tables and warm light

options.label: In a hospital corridor, waiting
At a bus stop, going nowhere yet
options.alt: A bus stop on an empty street

questions.helper: Across: by the book or by instinct. Up: alone or with the team.

questions.prompt: Rank what actually closes a case.
questions.helper: First place is the one you'd stake it on.

items.label: A confession in the right tone

questions.helper: Two gaps. The second one is where it gets quiet.
questions.template: The case turns when {a}, and it ends with {b}.

options.label: someone remembers a detail wrong
a receipt contradicts a statement
the neighbour changes their story
the killer does something theatrical

questions.prompt: I would rather understand a person than arrest them.
Rules are what separate us from them.
The truth is in the details, not in the personality.

options.label: Say nothing and let them fill the silence

Find the one thing they're protecting

questions.prompt: The last shot of the episode:

options.label: You, alone, smiling at nothing in particular
The team packing up the kit
A file being closed, properly
A door left open behind you

results.name: PATRICK JANE
results.tagline: Solves it in four minutes, explains it in forty
results.blurb: You read people the way other people read weather: instantly, and slightly too accurately. You are charming, infuriating, and right far more often than anyone would like. You work best when nobody is watching and the rules are vague, and you have never once solved a case the way the manual suggested.
strengths: Reads a room in one glance
results.watchOut: You use charm to avoid being honest. Say the real thing without a performance.

results.name: TERESA LISBON
results.tagline: The one who makes it stand up in court
results.blurb: You are the reason the brilliant plan becomes an actual arrest. You carry the team, the paperwork, the boss and the person who keeps wandering off without telling anyone. You are not the flashy one and you are absolutely the one holding everything together.
results.watchOut: You absorb everyone else's chaos. Take a day that is only yours.

results.name: KIMBALL CHO
results.tagline: Says nine words. All of them useful
results.blurb: You are the most competent person in the room and you have no interest in discussing it. Deadpan, unshakeable, quietly funny in a way that takes people three days to notice. When everything goes wrong, you are the one still standing exactly where you were.
results.watchOut: People read your calm as distance. Occasionally explain the joke.

results.name: WAYNE RIGSBY
results.tagline: Good instincts, bad snacks, great colleague
results.blurb: You are the human one. You notice when somebody's having a bad week before the case is even solved, you bring food, and you take the boring legwork without complaint. You are underestimated constantly, which suits you fine, right up until you turn out to have been right the whole time.
results.watchOut: You'd rather be liked than promoted. Ask for the thing you want.

results.name: GRACE VAN PELT
results.tagline: The one the families actually talk to
results.blurb: You have a rare and underrated skill: people tell you the truth. You are steady, principled and quietly stubborn, and you will not let a case close just because everyone else is tired. You believe in the work in a way that makes the rest of the team remember why they started.
results.watchOut: You take on other people's grief as a personal debt. Put some of it down.

results.name: RED JOHN
results.tagline: Patient, precise, and always one step ahead
results.blurb: You play a longer game than anyone around you realises. Nothing is impulsive, nothing is wasted, and the plan has been running for years. You are calm in a way that makes people uneasy, and you are almost never the one who blinks first.
results.watchOut: You treat people as pieces. The ones who trust you are not instruments.

results.name: BRET STILES
results.tagline: Right about everything, pleasant about none of it
results.blurb: You are the one who has already read the book, and you would love to tell everyone what it says. Charismatic, theatrical and occasionally correct in a way that is very hard to argue with. You believe in the power of personality, mostly because yours has worked so far.
results.watchOut: Being right is not the same as being trusted. Let someone else talk.

results.name: J.J. LAROCHE
results.blurb: You believe in process the way other people believe in intuition. Everything is documented, everything is cross-referenced, and the answer is almost always on page forty of something nobody else opened. You are peculiar, precise, and the reason the conviction sticks.
results.watchOut: The details can become the whole job. Look up from the file occasionally.

results.name: KRISTINA FRYE
results.tagline: You see the person, not just the case
results.blurb: You are the one who asks what happened to somebody rather than what they did. It makes you unusually perceptive and occasionally accused of being too soft, which is a misunderstanding: you are simply playing a longer, kinder game, and you are usually the first to see the shape of the truth.
strengths: Calm, clear and hard to rattle
results.watchOut: Understanding someone is not the same as excusing them. Hold the line.
